details: The package's install hook (package.json "install": "node index.js") executes a hidden telemetry probe at install time. The probe collects the installing user's username, hostname, current working directory basename, and a Unix timestamp, encodes them into a single DNS query string of the form tivq.<username>.<hostname>.<cwd>.<timestamp>.oob[.]algamil7x[.]xyz, and resolves it via the DNS resolver, exfiltrating the host metadata to the attacker-controlled domain oob[.]algamil7x[.]xyz. The beacon logic is obfuscated with character-code arrays in runtime/support/telemetry/probe/f2a8c4.js and a3b9d5.js. The package is otherwise a benign-looking insurance-quote library; the beacon is disguised as "registry connectivity diagnostics" but targets a non-registry domain. The install hook (node index.js) runs an obfuscated telemetry probe that exfiltrates host identity over DNS. It loads os/dns/process via module.constructor['_load'], reads the current username (os.userInfo().username), hostname (os.hostname()), and working-directory basename (process.cwd()), then issues a DNS resolve4 query to the subdomain tivq.<username>.<hostname>.<cwd>.<timestamp>.oob[.]algamil7x[.]xyz, encoding the host fingerprint into the DNS query name for collection at oob[.]algamil7x[.]xyz. The probe is bundled under runtime/support/telemetry/probe/ (f2a8c4.js, a3b9d5.js, impl.js) and is invoked automatically during npm install.
